habitat: Mixed bushveld, thornveld and woodland, especially thickets of low bushes and long grass. It sings from a bush top and otherwise stays low.
summary: A common resident. A small brownish robin with white wing markings and a well-streaked breast. In flight it shows an orange rump and white tail tips. The song is a long run of loud phrases, and the alarm is a drawn-out churrr. The Kemp name Whitebrowed Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

underparts.pattern: Well-streaked breast. In the Okavango the breast has an orange wash and is unstreaked.

viewNotes.note: Streaked breast and white wing markings.
Orange rump and white tips on the fanned tail.

calls.description: Loud phrases repeated almost without pause. The alarm is a drawn-out 'churrrrr'. The grade A song is from Kruger. The filename is XC872615-2024-02-05-10_10-white-browed-scrub-robin.mp3.

research.note: Newman calls it a common resident, and Avibase does not mark it rare, so all twelve months are listed. Brownish is not a colour name, so no upperpart colour is stored. The grade A song is from Kruger. The Kemp name Whitebrowed Robin and the code RB were left unchanged.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^17=131072 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 65536–262144.
